title: Direct and Indirect Object Pronouns
subtitle: mi, ti, lo, la, ci, vi, li, le. Position before verb or attached to infinitive.
objectives: Understand direct and indirect object pronouns.
Apply direct and indirect object pronouns in reading and composition.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body: This lesson covers direct and indirect object pronouns. Italian grammar builds on patterns you have already learned. Focus on recognizing forms in context before producing them.

sections.heading: From Italian literature
sections.body: Real examples from Dante, Petrarch, Boccaccio, Machiavelli, Leopardi, or Manzoni illustrate this grammatical point in living use.

items.prompt: What is the main function of direct and indirect object pronouns?
